memo:
EdgeHound Portfolio Review — 20 June 2026

The fund sits at -12.75% return on $10K starting capital, with equity at $8,725. The core SHORT_FAVORITE engine on sports markets remains the one validated edge: 72.2% win rate (38W/14L, CI 62-82%) across 52 qualified trades. This is the portfolio's only reliable alpha source and must be protected.

The critical problem is stake sizing volatility. Recent logs show $750 stakes on individual trades — Dota 2 Yakult Brothers (-$470), LoL Dplus KIA (-$503), Nottingham Open Golubic (-$750) — which are catastrophic single-event losses. The maxEventExposure was $600 at config time yet $750 trades appear, suggesting earlier configs allowed these sizes. The bank has absorbed ~$1,700+ in losses from three esports/tennis upset events, likely non-sports contexts where the validated edge does NOT apply. SHORT_FAVORITE's validated hypothesis is specifically 'high-priced sports markets' — esports and tennis upsets are structurally different from MLB/mainstream sports favorites and are eroding the validated alpha.

ELITE_FOLLOW on the Iran nuclear/diplomatic cluster shows a dangerous pattern: repeated same-event entries averaging $300-$500 per leg, with mixed outcomes and clear overconcentration on a single geopolitical narrative. The aenews2 wallet score (44%) warrants skepticism.

MOMENTUM remains disabled correctly (-$1,019, 21 trades, 38% win rate). SMART_CONSENSUS has only 1 trade — keep disabled. VOLUME_SPIKE is marginally positive ($190, 8/20 wins) — insufficient evidence to expand.

Recommendation: Hold kellyMult conservative, tighten maxEventExposure to protect against single large losses, keep pMin stable. No engine changes warranted.
